english.html: nor the second husband's <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>: nevertheless some, for the reason I have stated, are of this heresy, that one ought prudently to consider which of the two husbands the child better resembles <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>, inasmuch as one commonly sees it happen — and Galen, that excellent physician, so demonstrates it — that children closely take after their fathers and parents <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>. I am not unaware, either, that many are in this error, of thinking that illegitimate children and bastards more resemble the putative father (who is the husband), because the woman, they say, during the act of lechery incessantly thinks of the husband, fearing his coming <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>; and the imaginations, as we have proved above, give form to the child who at that point is conceived and engendered <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>. Nevertheless everyone can easily judge, both by experience (mistress of all things) and by the authority of grave and learned persons, of the contrary, and that, as Phocylides the Greek poet said, beds defiled by lechery do not make children like the husbands.

english.html: Whence Horace, praising the Emperor Augustus for having severely punished and repressed adultery, said among other things that by this means persons became more continent and chaste, and women made their posterity and lineage like the husband <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>.

notes.original: Horace au liu. iiij. des car mes. Ode V.
notes.gloss: Nullis polluitur casta domus stupris, / mos et lex maculosum edomuit nefas, / laudantur simili prole puerperae, / culpam poena premit comes. Coras's Nullus for Nullis.

english.html: The chaste house is polluted by no defilements; custom and law have tamed the spotted sin; mothers are praised for offspring like their sires; punishment follows hard upon guilt as its companion.

Moreover, we see that bastards resemble their true and natural father, not only in body and in the features and lineaments of the face, but also in manners and dispositions <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup>.
